thread:
alex.k: Heads up — we just received a DSAR erasure for user id 8a3f2. Need to confirm that deletion propagated to backups/snapshots. I think our nightly snapshot retention job missed a few older snapshots. tagging @tara.m @sam.infra @sara.legal

tara.m: Can you paste the DSAR id and affected resource types? I’ll check the DSAR tracker and escalation rules.

alex.k: DSAR ID dsar-2026-1031, target: user-generated docs bucket + related instance volumes. No legal hold flagged in the intake form.

sam.infra: On it. Quick question — are backups encrypted with customer-managed CMKs or our cross-account CMK? That changes deletion steps.

sara.legal: Not under legal hold as far as intake shows. No retention exception requested, and legal says GDPR erasure should proceed if data locatable. Confirm with infra before deleting backups.

josh.sre: If volumes were snapshotted, we can find snapshots by tag or by volume-id. Try this query (aws):
```
aws ec2 describe-snapshots --filters Name=tag:dsar-id,Values=dsar-2026-1031 Name=owner-id,Values=123456789012 --query 'Snapshots[].[SnapshotId,StartTime,Description,Tags]' --output table
```

sam.infra: Ran a search across regions. Found 3 candidate snapshots: snap-0a1b2c3d (us-east-1, 2025-11-02), snap-0f9e8d7c (eu-west-1, 2025-12-10), snap-01aa22bb (us-east-1, 2024-08-14). All encrypted with customer CMK arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01.

alex.k: Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) we need to ensure deletion of snapshots is recorded in audit logs (who/when/command). 2) KMS key access must allow deletion (CMK policy might block deletes if key admin locked). Sam, can you confirm key access?

sam.infra: Key policy shows our backup service principal has Describe and CreateGrant but not kafk? (typo) — it lacks explicit kms:ReEncrypt and kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion isn't relevant. For deleting encrypted snapshots we just need permission to delete snapshot resource; KMS is only used for encryption/decryption metadata. But we must record the key usage audit entry. I'll open a minimal-grant for the operator running the deletion and document the grant ID.

sara.legal: Please pause destructive steps if you find anything that indicates a cross-account snapshot share. We need to confirm no third-party holds.

josh.sre: Quick check for shares:
```
aws ec2 describe-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id snap-0a1b2c3d --attribute createVolumePermission
```
All three snapshots show no createVolumePermission entries beyond our account.

sam.infra: Okay, planning deletion sequence: 1) create audit entry in our DSAR tracker with planned deletion window, 2) create short-lived KMS grant for operator, 3) delete snapshots with aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id <id>, 4) capture CLI stdout/stderr and upload to secure audit log storage, 5) expire KMS grant.

alex.k: Sounds good. Please include a note about eventual propagation — if snapshots were used to create AMIs or copy to other regions, those copies need erasure too. Confirm copy/AMI search.

sam.infra: Found one AMI (ami-0c55aa33) in us-east-1 with block device mapping pointing to snap-01aa22bb. That AMI will need deregister + block device trajectory cleared before snapshot delete to avoid rehydration. I’ll deregister AMI first.

josh.sre: Also watch for backup catalog records (internal vault). If the catalog references snapshot ids, purge the catalog entry after deletion. That’s part of our data minimization doc.

sam.infra: Executing now. Commands I ran:
```
aws ec2 deregister-image --image-id ami-0c55aa33
aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id snap-01aa22bb
```
Deletion stdout: "Deleted snapshot snap-01aa22bb". Uploaded CLI log to s3://redwood-audit/dsar-2026-1031/logs/2026-03-10-1012.log

audit-bot: Audit entry created: dsar-2026-1031 | action=delete_snapshot | actor=sam.infra | resources=[snap-01aa22bb] | log=https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-audit/dsar-2026-1031/logs/2026-03-10-1012.log

sam.infra: Proceeding with the two remaining snapshots in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 (snap-0f9e8d7c, snap-0a1b2c3d). KMS grant created (grant-id: g-7f9a) valid 15 minutes. Running deletions now.

sam.infra: Deletion results: snap-0f9e8d7c -> "Deleted snapshot snap-0f9e8d7c"; snap-0a1b2c3d -> "Deleted snapshot snap-0a1b2c3d". Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-audit/dsar-2026-1031/logs/2026-03-10-1020.log

audit-bot: Audit entry created: dsar-2026-1031 | action=delete_snapshot | actor=sam.infra | resources=[snap-0f9e8d7c,snap-0a1b2c3d] | log=https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-audit/dsar-2026-1031/logs/2026-03-10-1020.log

sara.legal: Confirming receipt of audit links. From legal side this satisfies erasure proof for now. Please preserve logs in the secure archive.

tara.m: Moving follow-up into infra backlog: we need automation so DSAR intake triggers snapshot/AMI/catalog harvest + deletion where applicable, and add post-action audit steps. I’ll create a ticket and assign to sam.infra and devex to update runbook.

alex.k: Thanks everyone — good call on AMI check. Closing ticket once devex confirms runbook changes and audit retention archived. :white_check_mark:

josh.sre: small action item — can we add a lightweight check to the nightly snapshot retention job to mark snapshots linked to a DSAR tag so they auto-expire faster? Lowering blast radius of manual ops.

tara.m: Agree. Adding to ticket.

alex.k: Leaving this thread open for any post-mortem notes. Great job coordinating.
